Plot Hellinger enrichment contrasts with uncertainty.

Source: R/plot-composition-contrasts.R
PlotCompositionContrasts.Rd

Takes a HellingerEnrichmentResult and returns a ggplot with one row per pairwise contrast. By default the plot stacks two panels that share those rows: the between/within Hellinger ratio \(R\) on top and the energy distance \(E\) below, each with its own x axis, so both read left to right. \(R\) carries the p-values, PPGT1, and R_PPGTnope; \(E\) shows the size of the shift in squared Hellinger units. A dotted line marks each statistic's no-difference value (\(R = 1\), \(E = 0\)). Set showEnergyDistance = FALSE for the ratio alone.

Usage

PlotCompositionContrasts(
  result,
  theme = egg::theme_article(),
  showOmnibus = TRUE,
  showEnergyDistance = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

result

A HellingerEnrichmentResult from CompareGroupCompositions.

theme

ggplot2 theme (default egg::theme_article()). With the default, the legend sits above the panels; a theme you supply keeps its own legend placement.

showOmnibus

If TRUE, mark the omnibus value in each panel with a dashed line.

showEnergyDistance

If TRUE (default), stack an energy distance panel below the ratio panel.

...

Passed to ggdist::stat_halfeye for Bayes plots.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

Bayes results draw from the retained posterior draws (nPosterior rows per contrast) via ggdist::stat_halfeye, because a density slab needs samples rather than summarized intervals. Half-eye nested intervals follow result$settings$credibleInterval (HPDI via ggdist::mean_hdi, CPI via ggdist::mean_qi) unless ... overrides point_interval. When a Bayes result carries a NOPE, permutation-calibrated or fixed, a gray band behind each half-eye spans that statistic's interval: \(R\) from 1 to R_nopeHigh in the top panel, \(E\) from 0 to E_nopeHigh in the bottom panel. You can then see how much of each posterior clears its edge. The legend names each band: "NOPE (permutation)" for the default permutation-calibrated bound, whose band shows the median of the per-draw bounds, or "NOPE (fixed)" for a bound you supplied. Permutation results have no draws, so they render as points colored by adjusted significance. When showOmnibus is TRUE, a dashed line in each panel marks the omnibus value; the \(R\) panel labels it with its p-value (permutation) or PPGT1 and R_PPGTnope (Bayes), and the \(E\) panel labels it with \(E\) and, under Bayes, E_PPGTnope. Omnibus draws stay in result$omnibus$draws rather than as a plot row.
